idiom_name: plain-object filter documents (MongoDB-style) / chainable builder object (Knex)
implementation_notes: The query object is usually not a class but a plain data object: collection.find({status: 'active', qty: {$gt: 20}}) passes the query as data and the driver interprets it, and for SQL the same idea appears as a chainable builder object (Knex's query builder). What replaces the classic structure is the object literal plus a small interpreter, because JavaScript is structurally typed and needs no Query class hierarchy; a hand-written query wrapper stays justified when queries must be validated, frozen or serialised under a stable shape that a permissive driver object does not guarantee.
pitfalls: Passing a request body straight into the filter enables operator injection ($where, $ne): reshape and whitelist keys before building the object.
Filter objects are mutable: a shared literal that one caller extends changes every query using it - freeze or clone it.
The plain-object form carries no SQL parameter binding; mixing raw fragments (whereRaw) reopens the injection the structure avoided.
